Examine whether the operation * defined on R by $\mathrm{a} * \mathrm{~b}=\mathrm{ab}+1$ is (i) a binary or not.
(ii) if a binary operation, is it associative or not?
questions.solution:
As $a, b \in R \Rightarrow a b \in R \Rightarrow a b+1 \in R \Rightarrow a^* b \in R \Rightarrow *$ is binary. For associative $(a * b) * c=(a b+1) * c=(a b+1) c+1=a b c+c+1$ also, $\mathrm{a} *(\mathrm{~b} * \mathrm{c})=\mathrm{a} *(\mathrm{bc}+1)=\mathrm{a} \cdot(\mathrm{bc}+1)+1=\mathrm{abc}+\mathrm{a}+1$ In general $\left(a^* b\right)^* c
eq a^*\left(b^* c\right) \Rightarrow *$ is not associative.

questions.solution:
Let $\mathrm{e} \in \mathbb{R}$ be the identity element.
then $\mathrm{a}^* \mathrm{e}=\mathrm{e}^* \mathrm{a}=\mathrm{a}$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{a}^2+\mathrm{e}^2=\mathrm{e}^2+\mathrm{a}^2=\mathrm{a}^2 \Rightarrow \mathrm{e}^2=0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{e}=0 .$
$\therefore$ Identity element is $0 \in \mathbb{R}$

questions.q: Let $R$ be a relation defined over $N$, where $N$ is set of natural numbers, defined as " $m R n$ if and only if $m$ is a multiple of $n, m, n \in N$." Find whether $R$ is reflexive, symmetric and transitive or not.
questions.solution:
Let $x \in N$. Then we know that x is a multiple of itself.
$\Rightarrow x R x$
Hence, R is reflexive.
We have $2,8 \in N$ such that 8 is a multiple of 2
$\Rightarrow 8 R 2$
But, 2 is not a multiple of 8 . Hence, 2 is not R-related to 8 .
Therefore, R is not symmetric.
Let $x, y, z \in N$ such that $x R y, y R z$
Then $x=m y, y=n z$ for some $\mathrm{m}, n \in N$
$\Rightarrow x=m n z \Rightarrow x=p z$, where $p=m n \in N$. Hence, $x R z$
Therefore, R is transitive.

$f(x)=a x+b$

$f(x)=2 x-1$

An exhibit in the museum depicted many rail lines on the track near the railway station. Let $L$ be the set of all rail lines on the railway track and $R$ be the relation on $L$ defined by
$\mathrm{R}=\left\{\left(l_1, l_2\right): l_1\right.$ is parallel to $\left.l_2\right\}$

(i) Find whether the relation R is symmetric or not.
(ii) Find whether the relation R is transitive or not.
(iii) If one of the rail lines on the railway track is represented by the equation $y=3 x+2$, then find the set of rail lines in R related to it.
(iii)(b) Let S be the relation defined by $\mathrm{S}=\left\{\left(l_1, l_2\right): l_1\right.$ is perpendicular to $\left.l_2\right\}$ check whether the relation $S$ is symmetric and transitive.

(i) Let $\left(l_1, l_2\right) \in R \Rightarrow l_1\left\|l_2 \Rightarrow l_2\right\| l_1 \Rightarrow\left(l_2, l_1\right) \in R, \therefore R$ is a symmetric relation

(iii) The set is $\{1: 1$ is a line of type $y=3 x+c, c \in R\}$
(iii)(b)
Let $\left(1_1, 1_2\right) \in R \Rightarrow 1_1 \perp 1_2 \Rightarrow 1_2 \perp 1_1 \Rightarrow\left(1_2, 1_1\right) \in R, \therefore R$ is a symmetric relation Let $\left(1_1, 1_2\right),\left(1_2, 1_3\right) \in R \Rightarrow 1_1 \perp 1_2, 1_2 \perp 1_3 \Rightarrow 1_1 \| 1_3 \Rightarrow\left(1_1, 1_3\right)

questions.q: Prove that the relation R on Z , defined by $\mathrm{R}\{(\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{y}):(\mathrm{x}-\mathrm{y})$ is divisible by 5$\}$ is an equivalence relation.
questions.solution:
For reflexive $x-x=0$, for every $x \in Z$ is divisible by $5 \Rightarrow(x, x) \in R$ For symmetric $(x, y) \in R \Rightarrow x-y$ is divisible by $5 \Rightarrow y-x$ is divisible by 5 $\Rightarrow(y, x) \in R \Rightarrow R$ is symmetric.
For transitive Let $(x, y) \in R$ and $(y, z) \in R$
$(x, y) \in R \Rightarrow x-y=5 \lambda$
$(y, z) \in R \Rightarrow y-z=5 \mu$
$\operatorname{adding}(i)$ and $(i i), x-z=5(\lambda+\mu)=5 k \Rightarrow(x, z) \in R \Rightarrow R$ is transitive.
Hence $R$ is an equivalence relation.

questions.q: Show that the relation R in the set $\mathrm{A}=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}$ given by $\mathrm{R}=\{(\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}):|\mathrm{a}-\mathrm{b}|$ is divisible by 2$\}$ is an equivalence relation.
questions.solution:
Reflexive: $|\mathrm{a}-\mathrm{a}|=0$, which is divisible by 2 for all $\mathrm{a} \in \mathrm{A}$.
$\therefore \quad(\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{a}) \in \mathrm{R} \Rightarrow \mathrm{R}$ is reflexive.
Symmetric: Let $(\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}) \in \mathrm{R}$ i.e., $|\mathrm{a}-\mathrm{b}|=2 \lambda, \lambda \in \omega$ then $|\mathrm{b}-\mathrm{a}|=|-(\mathrm{a}-\mathrm{b})|=|\mathrm{a}-\mathrm{b}|=2 \lambda$
$\Rightarrow(b, a) \in R \Rightarrow R$ is symmetric.
Transitive : Let $(\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}),(\mathrm{b}, \mathrm{c}) \in \mathrm{R}$ i.e., $|\mathrm{a}-\mathrm{b}|=2 \lambda,|\mathrm{~b}-\mathrm{c}|=2 \mu$
$a-c=(a-b)+(b-c)= \pm 2 \lambda \pm 2 \mu= \pm 2(\lambda+\mu)$
$|\mathrm{a}-\mathrm{c}|=2|\lambda+\mu|$, which is divisible by 2
$\Rightarrow(\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{c}) \in \mathrm{R} \Rightarrow \mathrm{R}$ is transitive.
Hence $R$ is an equivalence relation.

questions.solution:
(i) Reflexive: $\forall \mathrm{a} \in \mathrm{A},|\mathrm{a}-\mathrm{a}|=0$ which is even $\Rightarrow(\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{a}) \in \mathrm{R}$, hence R is reflexive
(ii) Symmetric: Let $(\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}) \in \mathrm{R} \Rightarrow|\mathrm{a}-\mathrm{b}|$ is even $\Rightarrow \mathrm{I}-(\mathrm{b}-\mathrm{a}) \mid$ is even $\Rightarrow \mid \mathrm{b}-\mathrm{al}$ is even so, $(b, a) \in R$ hence R is symmetric.
(iii) Transitive: Let $(\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}),(\mathrm{b}, \mathrm{c}) \in \mathrm{R}$ so, $\mid \mathrm{a}-\mathrm{bl}$ is even and $\mid \mathrm{b}-\mathrm{cl}$ is even $\Rightarrow \mathrm{a}-\mathrm{b}=2 \lambda, \mathrm{~b}-\mathrm{c}=2 \mu$ where $\lambda, \mu \in \mathrm{Z}$ Now, $\mathrm{a}-\mathrm{c}=(\mathrm{a}-\mathrm{b})+(\mathrm{b}-\mathrm{c})=2(\lambda+\mu) \Rightarrow \mathrm{la}-\mathrm{cl}$ is even, so $(\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{c}) \in \mathrm{R}$ hence $R$ is transitive.
Since $R$ is reflexive, symmetric and transitive therefore its an equivalence relation
